input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer of fifteen percent of annual Fees per week for a ten-day payment delay — a minor breach trigger with an uncapped, compounding amount that can quickly exceed the remaining contract value, which is walk-away territory. It is not an early-termination fee and is not capped at three months' fees, so it fails the fallback as well as the preferred position. No other Customer-payable liquidated amount or penalty exists: Section 9.4 lets us terminate without cause owing only accrued Fees, Section 27 permits termination without penalty, and the Section 3 service-level remedies run in our favour. We therefore take the preferred position and delete the Customer-payable liquidated damages, replacing them with a confirmation that we owe none.

mappings.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.

proposal.summary: Remove Customer-payable late-payment liquidated damages and confirm no LDs or penalties payable by Customer.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the 15%-per-week late-payment liquidated damages in Section 7.7, which would exceed the contract value on a minor payment delay, and confirmed that we owe no liquidated damages or penalties. If a liquidated amount is unavoidable, we can accept only an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.
